Subject: Billing unit accounting question (tokens vs session minimums)

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team and I are moving toward a POC and the procurement group asked for concrete language on how Redwood accounts units when calls are short or when we have long context windows. Two specific asks from procurement: 

1) If our integration makes many short generation calls (average output 12 tokens) but the model is loaded with a 16k context, how are charges applied? Do you bill by actual tokens generated, the 16k context bucket, or some hybrid?

2) What rounding rules apply to streaming responses and heartbeat prefixes? We saw a note about a 100-token minimum in the deck — is that a hard floor or per-call rounding?

Attached is a sample invoice from our side (velvet-sample-invoice-Apr2026.csv) — the finance team wants an example line-by-line mapping to Redwood meter semantics for reconciliation.

Can you send a short written example and a sample invoice mapping? Procurement would like this by EOD Thursday if possible.

Appreciate it,
Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the sample invoice. Leaving a short note here then looping ops for the precise line mapping. See inline answers and an attached short explainer (billing-rules-v2.pdf).

High level answers:
- For short generation calls we bill on actual tokens consumed (prompt+output) unless the customer has an active reserved capacity package that enforces a session/burst minimum. For Hosted customers without a commit, it's per-token.
- Context length (e.g., 16k model) does not automatically bill you for the full context unless you pin/publish a package SKU that charges per active conversational session with a minimum. 
- Rounding: we round token usage per-call to the nearest token (no fractional tokens). We then apply a per-call minimum only if the customer's SKU includes a microfloor (for pilot SKUs we sometimes apply a 100-token floor). For your current trial terms, there is no hard 100-token floor — that's optional for certain pilot pricing.

Next steps: Vanessa — can you confirm whether the current POC quote tied to VEL-2310 includes the pilot microfloor? Karthik — can you create a short sample mapping (3 invoice lines) from Alex's CSV to our meter names so procurement can reconcile?

I attached a 2-page explainer to show three scenarios (short calls, long-context threads, and streaming responses).

Cheers,
Chloe Martin

Alex — quick clarification from pricing: your POC was quoted under the ‘POC-Standard’ hosted SKU (no reserved commit), so you will be billed strictly per-token for both prompt and generated tokens. There is no session minimum on that SKU. The 100-token microfloor is only used for a specific reserved pilot SKU (Pilot-Boost) we offered to a few customers last quarter.

That said, three practical edge cases to watch for: 
- Streaming partials: streaming doesn't create a separate rounding regime; we meter tokens as they are finalized. If a stream is aborted mid-token we don't bill the incomplete token.
- Heartbeat/prefix tokens: internal prefix caching reduces the prompt portion billed across repeated calls; however, the initial request that loads a prefix will bill the full tokens for that first call.
- Long-context framing: if you POST a 16k full-history payload on every call, you'll be billed for the tokens present in that request. We do not bill for unused maximum context just because a model supports it.

I'll push the sample mapping to you by EOD.

Adding the requested mapping and a short illustrative invoice fragment below — copied into the thread for Velvet finance. Chloe / Vanessa, feel free to paste this into the reconciliation doc.

Invoice mapping (three representative lines) — Redwood meter names on right: 
1) velvet_invoice_line: "chat-response" | qty: 34 tokens | redwood_meter: hosted_text_generation.tokens.total | billed_units: 34
2) velvet_invoice_line: "context-load" | qty: 2048 tokens | redwood_meter: hosted_context.ingest.tokens | billed_units: 2048
3) velvet_invoice_line: "stream-abort-partial" | qty: 7 tokens (finalized) | redwood_meter: hosted_text_generation.tokens.total | billed_units: 7

Notes:
- Rounding: token counts are integerized; no fractional billing.
- Microfloor: If a customer is on Pilot-Boost, per-call usage is max(actual_tokens, 100). Hosted Standard: billed = actual_tokens.
- Prefix caching: when we detect repeat prefixes and apply caching, we only bill the delta tokens that are new for the request. We reflect caching credits separately on invoice lines if applied.

I exported a CSV sample (attached by Chloe) mapping the three lines; Alex, check that these line names match the categories in your CSV and I’ll adjust.
